scope: Proposition 3.6 (Weighted linear forms) of the manuscript “Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers” (preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 164 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ab835f6a98c10d6d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 16-17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the number q of rows, the number d of base variables, and a bound b on the number of raw factors in each divisor. For each u ∈ [q], let σu be a product of at most b independent harmonic W-unit variables at the master cutoffs 16 of Lemma 3.3, and write νu(y) = Eσu1σu|y. All these raw draws are independent across occurrences. Suppose σu ≤ V surely, where V ≥ M → ∞. Let p consist of independent prime slots from finitely many gaps, each having Vl ≥ V . These slots are independent of all divisor draws. Let G be a domain depending only on p, and let ℓu(x; p) be homogeneous linear rows. On G their arguments are integers on the base sampling support. Assume the following conditions. 1. Given p and any possible divisor draws, the joint residue law of x modulo K = ∏︁q u=1 σu differs in total variation by at most ϵbase from the uniform law on (Z/KZ)d. The bound is uniform on G. 2. For every w < p ≤ V , each row is nonzero modulo p on G. There is a fixed finite list of nonzero integer polynomials in the prime slots such that, if all their values are nonzero modulo p, every pair of rows is linearly independent over Fp. The CRT law of all prime slots at the primes w < p ≤ V is within total variation ϵCRT of independent uniform units, with independence also across these primes. Then, uniformly in every further prime-only event E ⊆ G, Ep,x1E(p) q ∏︂ u=1 νu(ℓu(x; p)) = P(E) + O (︃ 1 w + V q (ϵbase + ϵCRT) )︃ . (3.11) The error is absolute, so the statement also applies when P(E) tends to zero. The implied constant depends only on the fixed row and divisor templates and polynomial tests. In particular the error is o(1) with the scales of Lemma 3.3 and base residue errors smaller than every fixed inverse power of V . Rows may have rational coefficients if their denominators are units modulo every possible divisor: interpret their residues by inverting those denominators. The integer-value and row hypotheses must still hold. Clearing such denominators leaves the congruence calculation unchanged. In particular this permits smooth denominators and prime pool denominators larger than V .
